artists.biography: The Farm are a British band from Liverpool. Their debut album Spartacus reached the top position on the UK Albums Chart when it was released in March 1991, featuring 2 songs which had been top 10 singles the year before. In 2012 they toured with their Spartacus Live shows, and formed part of The Justice Tonight Band, supporting The Stone Roses at Heaton Park, Phoenix Park, Lyon and Milan. The Justice Collective reached the Christmas Number One spot in 2012 with their recording of "He Ain't Heavy, He's My Brother".

perplexity.description:
Spartacus is the debut studio album by British band The Farm, released on 4 March 1991 through Produce Records. Musically, the album blends indie rock with electronic elements, drawing from the acid house and rave scenes of the late 1980s and early 1990s. This fusion is evident in tracks like "Groovy Train" and "All Together Now," which combine guitar-driven pop with danceable rhythms and club-oriented production, reflecting the band's Liverpool roots and the era's shifting musical landscape.

As The Farm's first full-length release, Spartacus marked a significant moment in their career, establishing their signature sound and earning them mainstream recognition. The album debuted at number one on the UK Albums Chart, propelled by the success of its singles and the band's energetic live performances. Its critical and commercial reception was strong, with praise for its innovative mix of rock and electronic styles, and it remains a defining work of the early 1990s UK indie-dance crossover movement.
